description: An oil and gas company operates on 300 acres of land where they use oil wells of small and large size. Per acre of land, a small oil well can produce 2 barrels of oil. Per acre of land, a large oil well can produce 5 barrels of oil. However, a small oil well produces 10 units of pollution and requires 5 drill bits per acre and a large oil well produces 20 units of pollution and requires 10 drill bits per acre. The company has available 2500 drill bits and due to strict environmental laws can produce at most 4500 units of pollution. For how many acres should each oil well be used to maximize the total production of oil?

ProductionPerAcre.definition: Oil production per acre for each well type

PollutionPerAcre.definition: Pollution generated per acre for each well type

DrillBitsPerAcre.definition: Drill bits required per acre for each well type

objective.description: "The goal is to maximize the total production of oil from the allocated acres of small and large oil wells."

constraints.description: The total acres allocated to small and large oil wells must not exceed the total available land (300 acres)
The total pollution generated by small and large oil wells must not exceed 4500 units
The acres allocated to each type of oil well must be non-negative

Acres.definition: Number of acres allocated to each type of oil well
